processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Spherical Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder (particle diameter 15–53 μm) was PREP-prepared using equipment from Advanced Corporation for Materials and Equipments (PREP-22). The PREP-prepared powder was cooled relatively slowly, so a small amount of carbon remained dissolved in the α-Fe phase.

structures.overall_structure: Highly spherical Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder with no satellites or irregular particles; solid (non-hollow) particles; Fe, Mn, Al and Ni uniformly distributed across particles.

defects.type: no internal pores or hollow core; particles are solid

characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the particle-size distribution of the PREP-prepared Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder
characterization_methods.key_findings: Particles mainly distributed in the 15–53 μm range; median particle size (D50) = 35.69 μm; unimodal, narrow distribution.

characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the flowability of the PREP-prepared powder
characterization_methods.key_findings: Powder exhibited excellent flowability with a Hall value of 14 s/50 g, suitable for SLM.

characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the crystal structure / phase constitution of the powder
characterization_methods.key_findings: Diffraction peaks for both γ-Fe(M) and α-Fe(M) phases; γ-Fe(M) dominates.

characterization_methods.technique: scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with EDS elemental mapping
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe powder morphology, element distribution, and particle cross-section
characterization_methods.key_findings: Powder is highly spherical with no satellites or irregular particles; Fe, Mn, Al and Ni are uniformly distributed; cross-section reveals solid particles (no hollow/pores). The C distribution was not mapped because the conductive tape contains a large amount of C.

unmapped_findings: Powder particle diameter is 15–53 μm and the median particle size (D50) was determined to be 35.69 μm (Fig. 3).
Powder flowability: Hall value of 14 s/50 g, which is suitable for SLM.
The PREP-prepared Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder is highly spherical with no satellites or irregular particles observed, and lacks hollow particles.
The particle-size distribution is unimodal and narrow, consistent with the reported good flowability.
The cross-sectional image of a particle reveals the solid nature of the powder, showing a cellular/dendritic solidification network and a distinct outer rim, with no internal pores.
Elemental C distribution is not included in the EDS maps because the conductive tape holding the powder contains a large amount of C.

γ-Fe(M) phase dominates because the PREP-prepared powder was cooled relatively slowly, resulting in a small amount of carbon dissolved in the α-Fe phase that promotes the formation of the ferrite phase.
Chemical composition of the Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni powder (ICP-OES, wt%): Mn 29.95, Al 8.63, C 1.20, Ni 3.45, O 0.01, Fe Bal. (Table 1).
